title: Near-duplicate students
prompt_md:
Some students appear twice in `students_raw` with the **same `student_id`** but slightly different text — different casing, stray spaces, an upper-cased email. (Other students appear twice as exact copies.)

List the `student_id`s (as integers) that have more than one row **where the rows are not identical**, sorted ascending. Return one column `student_id`.

example.input_md: `' Omar'` vs `'OMAR'` and `'omar@…'` vs `'OMAR@…'` are near-duplicates; two byte-identical rows are not.

hints: SQL: `GROUP BY student_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 AND COUNT(DISTINCT first_name || '|' || last_name || '|' || email) > 1`.
pandas: rows sharing an id → `duplicated('student_id', keep=False)`; then drop the ones that are full duplicates with `duplicated(keep=False)`.

starter.sql:
SELECT CAST(student_id AS INTEGER) AS student_id
FROM students_raw
GROUP BY student_id
HAVING 
ORDER BY student_id

solution.sql:
SELECT CAST(student_id AS INTEGER) AS student_id
FROM students_raw
GROUP BY student_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
   AND COUNT(DISTINCT first_name || '|' || last_name || '|' || email) > 1
ORDER BY student_id
solution.pandas:
multi = students_raw[students_raw.duplicated('student_id', keep=False)]
near = multi[~multi.duplicated(keep=False)]
result = pd.DataFrame({'student_id': sorted(near.student_id.astype(int).unique())})

title: Standardise home_state and count per state
prompt_md:
`home_state` in `students_raw` is a mess: `MO`, `Missouri`, `mo.`, `' MO'`, `Ill.`, `Illinois`, …

Standardise it to the two-letter code (trim spaces and trailing periods, upper-case, and map these full names: Missouri, Illinois/Ill, Kansas, Texas, California, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Indiana, Ohio, Tennessee). Then count **distinct students** per state.

Return `state`, `n_students`, ordered by `n_students` descending, then `state`.

example.input_md: SQLite: `TRIM(home_state, ' .')` strips spaces and dots from both ends. pandas: `.str.strip().str.strip('.').str.upper().replace({...})`.

hints: Canonicalise first (CTE / new column), then de-duplicate (student_id, state), then count.
A student's two rows may spell the state differently; after canonicalising they collapse into one.

starter.sql:
WITH canon AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT student_id,
    CASE UPPER(TRIM(home_state, ' .'))
      WHEN 'MISSOURI' THEN 'MO'
      -- more mappings
      ELSE UPPER(TRIM(home_state, ' .'))
    END AS state
  FROM students_raw
)
SELECT state, COUNT(*) AS n_students
FROM canon
GROUP BY state
ORDER BY n_students DESC, state

solution.sql:
WITH canon AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT student_id,
    CASE UPPER(TRIM(home_state, ' .'))
      WHEN 'MISSOURI' THEN 'MO' WHEN 'ILLINOIS' THEN 'IL' WHEN 'ILL' THEN 'IL'
      WHEN 'KANSAS' THEN 'KS' WHEN 'TEXAS' THEN 'TX' WHEN 'CALIFORNIA' THEN 'CA'
      WHEN 'WISCONSIN' THEN 'WI' WHEN 'MINNESOTA' THEN 'MN' WHEN 'INDIANA' THEN 'IN'
      WHEN 'OHIO' THEN 'OH' WHEN 'TENNESSEE' THEN 'TN'
      ELSE UPPER(TRIM(home_state, ' .'))
    END AS state
  FROM students_raw
)
SELECT state, COUNT(*) AS n_students
FROM canon
GROUP BY state
ORDER BY n_students DESC, state
solution.pandas:
names = {'MISSOURI': 'MO', 'ILLINOIS': 'IL', 'ILL': 'IL', 'KANSAS': 'KS', 'TEXAS': 'TX', 'CALIFORNIA': 'CA',
         'WISCONSIN': 'WI', 'MINNESOTA': 'MN', 'INDIANA': 'IN', 'OHIO': 'OH', 'TENNESSEE': 'TN'}
s = students_raw.copy()
s['state'] = s.home_state.str.strip().str.strip('.').str.upper().replace(names)
result = (s.drop_duplicates(['student_id', 'state']).groupby('state').size()
          .reset_index(name='n_students').sort_values(['n_students', 'state'], ascending=[False, True]))

title: Total posted payments, cleaned
prompt_md:

solution.sql:
WITH p AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT payment_id, amount, status FROM payments_raw
),
c AS (
  SELECT REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(amount), '$', ''), ',', ''), 'USD', ''), ' ', '') AS amt,
         LOWER(TRIM(status)) AS status
  FROM p
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(CAST(amt AS REAL)), 2) AS posted_total
FROM c
WHERE status = 'posted' AND amt GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(amt AS REAL) > 0 AND amt <> '9999'
solution.pandas:
p = payments_raw.drop_duplicates('payment_id')
amt = pd.to_numeric(p.amount.str.replace(r'[$,\sA-Za-z]', '', regex=True), errors='coerce')
ok = (amt > 0) & (p.amount.str.strip() != '9999') & (p.status.str.strip().str.lower() == 'posted')
result = pd.DataFrame({'posted_total': [round(float(amt[ok].sum()), 2)]})
